docs.title: 3A · Open the IDE and connect your API key
docs.text:
Goal: the assistant in the IDE answers you. Time: 5 minutes

The Test Suite IDE is one way to build a TCK project faster: blocks, a YAML editor and an AI assistant in the browser.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the address in box B of your handout and sign in with the account next to it.
  2. In the bar on the left, click the Test Suite IDE icon. The page is titled TCK Builder. You see the welcome screen.
  3. Download the template: e2e-test-template.zip.
  4. On the welcome screen, click Open File and choose the ZIP you just downloaded.
  5. At the top right, click Ask AI.

  6. Under Model, choose the model you brought:

    You brought Choose Then enter An OpenAI key A GPT model Your key, then Connect OpenAI An Anthropic key A Claude model Your key, then Connect Anthropic Catena-X AI access Catena-X AI Your key and agent ID

  7. Type Hello. What is in this project? and press Enter.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
The template project on the left, with its two tests, and the assistant panel on the right.

After step 7, the assistant answers with a short description of the two tests.

Note

Your key goes from your browser straight to the provider you chose. The Test Suite has no server for the assistant. Without Keep this key on this computer, the key is forgotten when you close the tab.

Tip

Stuck?

  • A "Welcome" dialog covers the page: close it with the × at its top right.
  • The key is refused: copy it again without spaces. A ChatGPT or Claude subscription is not an API key.
  • No API key, but a subscription to an AI coding assistant: take route C. You build on your laptop with your own tool and open the result here.
  • Nobody in the team has a model: join a team that has one, or build by hand from the worked example.

docs.text: The tutorial · chapter 3, route B · ● ● ● ○ ○ ○ ○ ○

docs.title: 3B · Connect a local model
docs.text:
Goal: a model on your own laptop answers you in the IDE. Time: 10 minutes, plus the download

The model runs on your laptop, so nothing leaves your machine. The IDE's Small model mode gives it short instructions and lets it look up what it needs, so even a small model answers in seconds.

docs.title: Which model?
docs.text:
Your laptop Take Download 8 GB of RAM qwen2.5:3b 2 GB 16 GB of RAM qwen2.5:3b or qwen2.5:7b 2 or 5 GB 32 GB or more, Apple Silicon or a large GPU A larger model, for example qwen2.5:14b or qwen3:30b 9 to 18 GB

In our trial, qwen2.5:3b and qwen2.5:7b both made every change the tutorial needs. Take the 3B unless your laptop has room to spare. The larger ones we have not tried. On a laptop without a GPU, expect a minute per step: route A or C is the better choice there.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama.

  2. Download the model. Best at home, before the session:

    ollama pull qwen2.5:3b

  3. Start Ollama so that the IDE may call it. Put the address from box B of your handout in place of the example:

    OLLAMA_ORIGINS="https://ide.example.org" OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve

  4. Open the address in box B and sign in. Click the Test Suite IDE icon on the left.

  5. Download the template, e2e-test-template.zip, and open it with Open File on the welcome screen.
  6. At the top right, click Ask AI. Under Model, choose Local / self-hosted LLM. Keep Server at Ollama and click Connect.
  7. Choose your model in the list. Leave Small model mode switched on.
  8. Type Hello. What is in this project? and press Enter.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text: After step 8, the assistant answers with a short description of the two tests, within half a minute.

docs.title: How to talk to a small model
docs.text:
You will use these in chapter 4:

  • One change per message. "Rename the step", then "add a check". Not "write the test".
  • Name the file every time: In tests/partner_uses_my_product.yaml …. Each message stands alone; the model does not remember the previous one.
  • Read every change. Each one is listed above the message box with Review and Undo.

Note

Small model mode is new. If your IDE does not show the switch yet, a local model needs OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 and a fast machine, and the first answer takes minutes. Then take route A or C.

Tip

Stuck?

  • "Could not load the server's models": Ollama is not running, or the address in OLLAMA_ORIGINS is not exactly the IDE's address. Stop it and start it again (step 3).
  • It answers but never changes a file: you are in Ask or Plan. Switch to Agent.
  • It keeps getting it wrong: ask for a smaller change, or switch to route A or C.

docs.title: 4 · Build the test with the assistant
docs.text:
Goal: a test project for your product that compiles. Time: 15 minutes

You say what must be proven. The assistant writes how. The Skeptic reads every line.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Compile at the top. The template compiles as it is: you start from green.
  2. In the assistant panel, switch the mode to Plan. A plan changes nothing.
  3. Paste starter prompt 1 and fill in your product, its repository and your sentence from chapter 2. Send it.

  4. Read the plan. The Skeptic asks three questions:

    Question A good plan says Does each test prove a promise? What the partner gets, not just "status 200" Is the negative test really a refusal? The exact answer the product must give Are addresses and BPNs variables? Nothing from your handout appears in a test

  5. Correct the plan in plain words until you agree with it.

  6. Press Carry out this plan. The assistant switches to Agent and writes the files.
  7. In the bar Changes by the AI assistant, press Review and read what changed. Undo file and Undo all put things back.
  8. Press Compile.

  9. Not green? Send this, and repeat until it is:

    Compile the project and fix what the compiler reports. Change nothing else.

  10. Press Save, give the draft your product's name, and press Save draft.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
The message Compilation passed, and your tests in the explorer on the left.

What the pilot team built Three tests for the Digital Twin Registry: | Test | Kind | | --- | --- | | A registered twin can be read back and matches the AAS schema | Positive, contract | | A partner finds and reads the twin through the owner's connector | Positive, the journey | | A twin that does not exist is answered with 404 | Negative | Read them in the [worked example](../reference/worked-example.md).

Note

On route B, with a local model: send one change per message and name the file in each one, for example In tests/partner_uses_my_product.yaml rename the step call_product to "Partner calls my product". A whole test in one message is too much for a small model.

Tip

Stuck?

  • The assistant invents steps: say Use only steps from the block catalog.
  • Compile stays red after three rounds: switch to Ask, paste the finding and ask what the compiler expects there, before you let it edit again.
  • Minute 30 and still red, or no model at all: press Undo all and change only the names by hand. Click a file, open the YAML Editor tab, press Edit, replace my-product with your product's id and My Product with its name, and press Save. Do it in index.yaml and in both tests. A small green test beats a large red one.
  • More prompts: Starter prompts.

docs.title: 5 · Run it against your connectors
docs.text: The tutorial · chapter 5 of 8 · ● ● ● ● ● ○ ○ ○

docs.title: 5 · Run it against your connectors
docs.text: Goal: a green run, and one red run that you caused on purpose. Time: 10 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Run at the top. The dialog Run to debug opens with five steps.

    Step You do Build Nothing. It ends with "Compiled — ready to run." Press Next. Infrastructure Choose your product under App under test and your connector under EDC Connector. If your test uses a registry, choose it under Digital Twin Registry. Press Next. Variables Click each value in the list. Fill in what is empty from box C of your handout: product_internal_url is "Product, as the connector reaches it", dtr_internal_url is "Registry, as the connector reaches it". Where the dialog offers a list, choose from it. Press Next. SUT Setup Press Start review, then Accept all and Confirm all. Your test creates these offers itself, in its setup. Press Next. Summary & Launch Check the list of tests. Press Run at the bottom right.

    You type nothing from box D. The partner side is set up by the administrators.

  2. Watch the Console at the bottom. Each step turns green or red as it finishes.

  3. Wait for the result.
  4. Now break it on purpose. Open your negative test, change the expected value of one check, for example 0 to 1 or 404 to 200, and run again.
  5. See it turn red at that check. Change it back and run once more.

A test that has never failed has proven nothing yet. Step 4 is the difference between a test and a script that prints green.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
The last step of the dialog, with your tests and your connector listed, and after the run the status Passed.

The second step, Infrastructure, looks like this when your components are registered:

Note

Nothing to choose under Infrastructure? Register it yourself, with the values of box C: Register an app (name and version of your product), Register a connector (name, DSP URL, Participant ID and DID) and Register a registry (name and base URL).

Tip

Stuck?

  • The run fails at once with "requires infrastructure that is not fully bound: engine.connector": the partner side is not set up for your team. Go to the Desk.
  • The run waits: give it a minute, then ask at the Desk whether your connectors are up.
  • A value is refused as "not a public host name": use the address from box C exactly as printed.
  • A step is red: open it and read the request and the answer. Decide which it is:
    • The environment. Nothing answered, or a value is wrong. Fix the value or ask.
    • A finding. The product answered, and not as your check expects. Either your reading of the promise is wrong, or the product is. Both are worth knowing.
  • Minute 40 and no green run: go on to chapter 6. The workflow runs your test again in CI, in a dataspace of its own.

docs.title: 6 · Add it to your repository
docs.text: The tutorial · chapter 6 of 8 · ● ● ● ● ● ● ○ ○

docs.title: 6 · Add it to your repository
docs.text: Goal: your test and the workflow that runs it are committed on a branch of your fork. Time: 10 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the IDE, click the ☰ menu at the top right, then File, then Export. In the dialog, press Export ZIP. The file lands in your downloads folder, named after your project.

  2. Open a terminal and clone the fork you made in chapter 2:

    git clone https://github.com/<your-user>/<your-product>.git
cd <your-product>
git switch -c test/e2e-test

  3. Unpack the ZIP into the folder tck/e2e:

    mkdir -p tck/e2e .github/workflows
unzip ~/Downloads/<your-project>.zip -d tck/e2e

  4. Add the workflow. It is the same for every product:

    BASE=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-tractusx/tutorial-resources/main/e2e-testing
curl -fsSL "$BASE/examples/digital-twin-registry/.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml" -o .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml

  5. In the same terminal, add the licence header to your test files. Eclipse projects need it on every file, and the IDE's export does not write it:

    curl -fsSL "$BASE/template/license-header.txt" -o /tmp/license-header.txt
for f in $(find tck/e2e -name '*.yaml'); do
  cat /tmp/license-header.txt "$f" > "$f.new" && mv "$f.new" "$f"
done

  6. Commit, with a sign-off:

    git add tck .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml
git commit -s -m "test: add an E2E test"

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
git show --stat HEAD

    test: add an E2E test

    Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.org>

 .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml               |  44 ++++
 tck/e2e/index.yaml                           | ...
 tck/e2e/tests/<your-first-test>.yaml         | ...
 tck/e2e/tests/<your-second-test>.yaml        | ...

And this is all the workflow is: a few lines that call a reusable workflow.

Tip

Stuck?

  • curl answers 404: the tutorial is not published at that address yet. Ask a facilitator for the address to use, also for the uses: line of the workflow file.
  • No unzip on your machine: unpack the ZIP with your file manager and move index.yaml and tests into tck/e2e.
  • Your repository already has a folder tck/e2e: choose another folder, and change tck-directory in the workflow file to match.
  • Your product does not run in the Umbrella: open .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml and add run-in-umbrella: false under tck-directory. The workflow then validates and compiles only. See The workflow.
  • Signed-off-by is missing: you forgot -s. Run git commit --amend -s --no-edit.

docs.title: 7 · Link it and open the pull request
docs.text: The tutorial · chapter 7 of 8 · ● ● ● ● ● ● ● ○

docs.title: 7 · Link it and open the pull request
docs.text: Goal: a draft pull request in your product's repository, with the test linked in .tractusx. Time: 5 minutes

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the file .tractusx in the root of your repository. It is the metafile that describes the product.

  2. Add this block at the end, with your product's name:

    e2eTests:
  - name: "<Your product> E2E test"
    path: "tck/e2e"
    workflow: ".github/workflows/e2e-test.yml"

  3. Commit and push:

    git add .tractusx
git commit -s -m "chore: link the E2E test in the metafile"
git push -u origin test/e2e-test

  4. Open your fork on GitHub. Press Compare & pull request in the yellow banner.

  5. Check that the base repository is eclipse-tractusx/<your-product>. Write one sentence per test: what it proves.
  6. Open the arrow next to the green button, choose Create draft pull request and press it.
  7. Ring the bell.

docs.title: You should now see
docs.text:
Your pull request, with the checks starting at the bottom: Validate and compile finishes in under a minute, Run in Tractus-X Umbrella in about five.

Click the second job and scroll to E2E test result. This is the pilot team's:

TCK RUN SUMMARY
  ✓ Register and read                          PASS
  ✓ A partner reads through the connector      PASS
  ✓ An unknown twin is not found               PASS
RESULT: PASS  |  3 passed  0 failed  0 skipped

Note

The first contribution of a person to a repository needs a committer's approval before its workflows run. If your checks say waiting for approval, that is the reason, not an error. A facilitator knows who can approve.

Tip

Stuck?

  • You want to see it run now: open a second pull request inside your fork, from test/e2e-test to your fork's main. It needs no approval and runs at once.
  • The ECA check is red: the email of your commits is not the one of your Eclipse account. See Troubleshooting.
  • git push is refused: GitHub wants a token or an SSH key, not your password. Let a teammate whose laptop can push be the Driver.
  • A check fails: Troubleshooting.

You have It means A TCK project in tck/e2e Your product's promise is written down in a form a machine can run A workflow It is checked on every pull request, in a fresh dataspace A link in .tractusx People and tools can find it A draft pull request The product's committers can take it from here

docs.title: Steps
